1415771873900568576 [2021-07-15] @QiaochuYuan 💜 4006 🔁 390 [(SEED) type=root]
a few days ago i took a medium dose of acid and wrote for several hours straight and admitted some things to myself, mostly about money

let's start here: last august my mom gave me $100,000 for my birthday. i resented her for this and also suppressed the resentment
├── 1415771875687362562 [2021-07-15] @QiaochuYuan 💜 417 🔁 12
│   in january i had the thought that i should "figure out money and career stuff" and then i proceeded to mostly avoid the topic, occasionally tentatively having feelings about it but not in a very satisfying way
│   
│   then i procrastinated on my taxes
│   ↓
│   1415771876706508802 [2021-07-15] @QiaochuYuan 💜 444 🔁 16
│   i procrastinated on my taxes so hard i was forced to spend the last day before the deadline mostly having feelings about taxes to find out why i had procrastinated so hard
│   
│   what came up was "i don't want to know how much money i have or made so i can't tell my parents about it"
│   ↓
│   1415771877792894977 [2021-07-15] @QiaochuYuan 💜 441 🔁 10
│   "and i don't want to tell my parents about my money situation because i don't want them to feel like they failed me"
│   
│   thinking that thought made me break into tears uncontrollably - like i want to clarify that this is rare for me, usually i can turn it off if i want to
│   ↓
│   1415771878900207618 [2021-07-15] @QiaochuYuan 💜 497 🔁 14
│   so that was progress. i learned that my feelings about money are intimately tied to my feelings about my parents. i went on to successfully avoid the topic again for another several weeks
│   
│   then i had to move out of my group house
│   ↓
│   1415771879948783617 [2021-07-15] @QiaochuYuan 💜 317 🔁 10
│   there was nowhere in particular i wanted to move to so i ended up moving into an airbnb which wasn't very good (too close to a busy street). towards the end of my stay i decided to take a medium dose of acid to see if it could get me unstuck on stuff and. hoo boy
│   ↓
│   1415771881005748226 [2021-07-15] @QiaochuYuan 💜 414 🔁 10
│   i wrote for maybe 12 hours straight and it eventually turned into a sort of spontaneous dialogue between the person i am on acid and the person i am sober; acidQC and soberQC
│   
│   acidQC told me a bunch of things i needed to hear but didn't particularly want to
│   ↓
│   1415771882024935425 [2021-07-15] @QiaochuYuan 💜 491 🔁 16
│   he told me "you've been feeling social pressure to pretend like you have a 'financial health' that is entirely about your savings and your income and it's just not true at all. the truth is that if you ran out of money your parents would send you more because they love you"
│   ↓
│   1415771883127992320 [2021-07-15] @QiaochuYuan 💜 523 🔁 16
│   "the truth is that your finances aren't separate from your parents' finances and they never have been. you resent your mom for sending you $100,000 because she forcefully reminded you of this fact"
│   ↓
│   1415771884117848066 [2021-07-15] @QiaochuYuan 💜 803 🔁 46
│   "you feel like you were told by society that the way making a living works is that you do labor and are paid a fair wage for your labor and that's how you earn the right to exist and be a member of society. you feel guilty because you've never done this"
│   ↓
│   1415771885111939072 [2021-07-15] @QiaochuYuan 💜 781 🔁 45
│   "but that's just not true. you actually do not need to earn the right to exist and you never have. the reason you're alive right now and not starving to death on the street even though you haven't had a job in 3 years is because your parents send you money because they love you"
├── 1415798941380132868 [2021-07-15] @nopranablem 💜 3
│   @QiaochuYuan Thanks for your openness! There's a lot of good stuff here that's making me think about my own relationship with money & my parents
│   
│   It can be easy to get into "objectify"/comparison mode when thinking about money and this thread probs isn't helpful to people that are doing that
├── 1415838003042398208 [2021-07-16] @strangestloop 💜 30
│   @QiaochuYuan thanks a lot for sharing QC
│   
│   i’m curious to know if you have any thoughts on this proposition that’s been rolling around in my head for a while and seems relevant:
│   
│   “any adult who is capable of taking care of themself ought to take care of themself.”
│   ↓
│   1415841646298615814 [2021-07-16] @QiaochuYuan 💜 15
│   @strangestloop the word "capable" is doing almost all of the work there it really depends on what that means ¯\_(ツ)_/¯ well "ought" too but let's start with "capable"
│   ↓
│   1415843523614674949 [2021-07-16] @strangestloop 💜 9
│   @QiaochuYuan true, most all of the words and phrases i consider to describe what I have in mind are pretty loaded, we could dance around meanings for a while. maybe eli5 gets to the heart of it:
│   
│   “for the good of society, if you can make enough money to take care of yourself, you should.”
│   ↓
│   1415844533728780291 [2021-07-16] @QiaochuYuan 💜 10
│   @strangestloop the word "can" is still doing a lot of work here (also "should"). there's really a lot wrapped up in the question of what it means to say you can or can't do something. like, to be explicit, it's not at all clear whether i "can" hold down a full-time job
│   ↓
│   1415844712213139457 [2021-07-16] @QiaochuYuan 💜 14 🔁 1
│   @strangestloop i don't have any physical disabilities preventing me from doing that but i do have... uh... a lot of trouble being a productive employee, in my experience. am in some sense disabled? should i be treated as such? no idea
│   ↓
│   1415847523068035083 [2021-07-16] @strangestloop 💜 6
│   @QiaochuYuan agreed on “can,” that can shift around as well based on factors like environment, illness, person-job fit
│   
│   your employee troubles are really surprising to me, though of course i’m operating off of not that much information - your podcasts with eigen mostly
│   ↓
│   1415849461478137859 [2021-07-16] @QiaochuYuan 💜 7
│   @strangestloop yeah in retrospect a lot of it might've come down to poor mentorship. i could potentially do a lot better with the right mentor but i'd still have to find something that seems worth doing
└── 1416063076709851137 [2021-07-16] @myhandle 💜 381 🔁 5
    @QiaochuYuan Thank you for writing this.
    
    The funniest thing about all the QTs saying they hate you while asking you for $$$ is that they all have the same neuroses and resentments around money but not the self-awareness to recognize and work on them.

1416333967448436738 [2021-07-17] @nowtheo 💜 14 🔁 2 [(SEED) type=quote_of_root]
A lot of people seem to be annoyed about the fact that QC needed LSD to come to very basic realizations.

They don't understand the nature of LSD and what "knowing" entails. Let's talk about it. 

(cont..) https://t.co/MRN1S0Q2Lo
  [Quoting @QiaochuYuan: a few days ago i took a medium dose of acid and wrote for several hours straight and admitted some things to myself, mostly about money  let's start here: last august my mom gave me $100,000 for my birthday. i resented her for this and also suppressed the resentment]
↓
1416333970250211330 [2021-07-17] @nowtheo 💜 13
We have reduced knowing to one thing — having justified true beliefs. And that's why our culture is so obsessed with ideologies. 

But that's just propositional knowing. And I guess at some level, QC propositionally knew all the things he outlined in the thread.
├── 1416333972217290756 [2021-07-17] @nowtheo 💜 10
│   What LSD perhaps enabled for him was a sense of perspectival and participatory knowing. 
│   
│   It enabled a transformation of not just his beliefs, but how he sees things. That's significant. 
│   
│   https://t.co/KhcMiPvHbm
│     [Quoting @nosilverv: Know thyself isn’t about propositional autobiographical knowledge 😭😭😭 it’s about stepping outside yourself, perspectival knowledge 😭😭😭😭 it’s a call to self transcendence 😭😭😭😭]
│   ↓
│   1416333974390018052 [2021-07-17] @nowtheo 💜 7
│   By de-centering, LSD allows you to break frame and see through the self-deceptive illusions of your mind. As a result, you can get a deep sense of connectedness with your emotions.
│   
│   You get to truly "know" yourself in a way that's not possible without altering your consciousness.
│   ↓
│   1416333981071527937 [2021-07-17] @nowtheo 💜 7
│   And to someone on the outside, the acid-fuelled insights might seem banal.
│   
│   But the person who is tripping is experientially realizing the importance and meaning of certain things — in ways you can't achieve through thinking or reading. https://t.co/h3UcktPncO
│   Images:
│     - [Image #0] The image is a quote about psychedelics, overlaid on a background photograph. 
│       
│       The quote, written in white text, reads: 
│       "Funny, I'd forgotten that what comes to you when you take a psychedelic is not always a revelation of something new and startling; you're more liable to find yourself reminded of simple things you know and forgot you knew - seeing them freshly - old, basic truths that long ago became cliches, so you stopped paying attention to them. ~ Author: Ann Shulgin"
│       
│       In the bottom-right corner, the website "quotessayings.net" is credited in small white text. The background image features a person holding a yellow umbrella, with their face obscured, standing in front of trees with yellow foliage.
│   ↓
│   1416333983311298560 [2021-07-17] @nowtheo 💜 8
│   That experiential realization, that participatory knowing is what it takes to fundamentally change your salience landscape. You realize how much bullshit there is in your life and mind. And you get good at filtering it out.
│   ↓
│   1416333985223905280 [2021-07-17] @nowtheo 💜 6
│   LSD is beautifully complex in the way it changes our mind's operations. There's so much going on.
│   
│   Of course, you also have to be careful:
│   
│   https://t.co/s9mLYavfMq
│     [Quoting @nowtheo: With psychedelics, there's a risk of getting caught up in our own bullshit.   Everything seems so profound, the meaningness is so enhanced, that we can end up having strong conviction in some random shit our mind came up with.   Gotta be vigilant.]
└── 1727477549306122327 [2023-11-23] @RomeoStevens76 💜 4 🔁 1
    @nowtheo Propositional knowing is a great phrase, and I'd say it usually stays contained on the social level. People can accurately report what propositions will be talked about as if they are true. This doesn't translate to what they will behaviorally predict.
